findings.title: Escaped trailing space in identifier is lost because the query is trimmed
findings.property: a selector built as '#' + escapeCssIdentifier(id) matches the element with that id
findings.expected: 1 element matched (an escaped space '\ ' is part of the identifier per CSS syntax)
findings.actual: 0 elements: the trailing escaped space is stripped when the query is trimmed, so the id parsed is 'a' followed by a dangling escape
findings.evidence: escapeCssIdentifier is documented to escape characters 'that would otherwise not be valid in a selector' (CSSOM serialize-an-identifier), so its output should be usable in a selector; it emits '\ ' for space, which select() then mishandles at the end of the query

review.title: Selector parsing drops an escaped trailing space because the query is trimmed first
review.reason: `QueryParser` calls `trimAsciiWhitespace(query)` before tokenizing, so the `\ ` that `Selector.escapeCssIdentifier("a ")` emits loses its space and leaves a dangling backslash. The public `escapeCssIdentifier` is documented to produce text valid in a selector, and CSS treats an escaped trailing space as part of the identifier. A maintainer would likely accept a small fix: only trim a trailing whitespace character when it is not preceded by an unescaped backslash. The case is narrow, since it needs an identifier that ends in whitespace.

fix.reason: the repro passes on the patched code
